title: Nine Groups
about: Spending two days manually balancing nine groups and realizing there had to be a better way to solve the problem.
description: This track remembers a deceptively simple assignment: divide everyone into nine balanced groups while accounting for all the constraints that made each placement affect the others. What sounded straightforward turned into two days of moving names, rewriting lists, and watching each solution create another conflict. Somewhere inside that frustration came a persistent thought: there had to be a better way. The task eventually became more than a scheduling puzzle, planting an idea about using systems and automation to solve problems that shouldn't have to be handled entirely by hand.
lyrics: They handed me a simple task,
At least that's how it seemed.
Nine different groups to build by hand,
Move one name and something else
Back and forth across the page,
Trying to make it all come out fair.
Move one person to the left,
Two whole days of moving names,
Just pages full of names and notes,
The more I tried to solve it,
There had to be a system
Was the start of something bigger.
"There has to be a better way."
Why should this be done by hand?
Maybe not as things now stand.
